maria: quick heads-up: on gpu-3 we've been seeing steady memory growth during long-context continuous-batching runs (~2h). p95 throughput stable but memory climbs ~3GB/hour. snippet from runtime log: `kv_allocs=1.21e6 kv_frees=9.6e5 kv_frag_ratio=0.41`

kevin: saw that too. ran off-host profiler for a 3h run. main signal is a rising number of small free slots that never get coalesced after batch-merge operations. seems like merging lots of short sequences into one 'meld' batch is creating many partial KV blocks -> fragmentation.

sophie: yup. hypothesis: when continuous-batching merges sequences, the head request in merged-batch often has the longest context and pins large contiguous kv ranges. backfills from later requests produce tiny free segments that allocator doesn't compact. over time fragmentation + small reuses -> growth. also observed head-of-line blocking when merge waits on eviction/gc.

maria: interesting. any repro commands we can run locally?

kevin: repro script:
```
./bench/continuous_batch.py \\  --model redwood-small \\  --seq-dist bimodal:64,2048 \\  --arrival poisson:50rps \\  --duration 7200 \\  --merge-threshold 0.7
```
Run with `--trace-kv` to dump per-batch allocations. I uploaded a trace to s3: s3://redwood-perf/kv/1773521120/trace.pb.gz

perf-bot: metric push: kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio=0.39, kv_merge_block_count=1124, kv_reuse_rate=0.62 (last 2h) :bar_chart:

dave: we saw correlated p99 latency regressions in prod canary around same time window. SRE paged the oncall yesterday because fallback to smaller model didn't trigger fast enough. we should prioritize a mitigation that avoids p99 spikes.

sophie: two ideas: 1) compact-on-merge: after batch meld, run a lightweight compaction that coalesces adjacent free slots if contiguous and under threshold; 2) cap merge length: don't allow a merged batch to exceed N token-positions (configurable). both are low-risk switches.

kevin: I prototyped compact-on-merge in my branch (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4032). local microbench shows fragmentation_ratio drop from 0.42->0.18 and memory slope goes close to flat for 3h runs. overhead ~1.5% CPU at merge time.

maria: nice. can we get perf counters first before enabling? add `kv_slot_count` and `kv_reuse_hit` per request so we can see reuse efficiency over time.

kevin: will do. adding counters + a flag `runtime.flags.kv_compact_on_merge` to gate the change. I'll also add `kv_merge_max_positions` flag to cap melded length.

dave: for quick prod mitigation set kv_merge_max_positions=4096 on canary pool, and enable compact flag only after a canary run. also turn up eviction-priority to favor tail-based frees (evict smallest contiguous segments first).

perf-bot: scheduled job: run microbench with PR/4032 on canary tonight 02:00 UTC, compare kv_* metrics and p99 across rollout windows.

sophie: small ask: instrument a histogram of "merge_wait_time" to see if eviction is causing HOL blocking. we saw some merges waiting multiple ms for GC to finish.

maria: agreed. action items: kevin -> push counters + PR 4032 updates (today); sophie -> add merge_wait_time histogram + dashboard panel; dave -> set canary flags and monitor p99; i'll coordinate the canary run and watch mem slope.

kevin: i'll post the updated trace and short README for repro in the PR. thanks all :thumbsup:

maria: perfect. if this looks good in canary we can schedule a gradual rollout with telemetry gating.

(THREAD END)
